stem: Which sentence makes a generalization about the vocabulary of creole languages?
stimulus:
Notes:
• A creole language forms when speakers of different languages build a shared language that children then learn as their first language.
• Most creole languages take much of their vocabulary from a single source language.
• Haitian Creole draws most of its vocabulary from French.
• Tok Pisin, spoken in Papua New Guinea, draws most of its vocabulary from English.
choices: Haitian Creole, a creole language, draws most of its vocabulary from French.
Most creole languages take much of their vocabulary from one source language.
Haitian Creole draws on French, while Tok Pisin draws on English instead.
All creole languages take their vocabulary from either French or English.
explanation: A generalization is a claim about the whole category, and no single language is its subject. Choice B is about "most creole languages" and names none of them, so it works at the category level. This is the first step in any Rhetorical Synthesis question whose goal says "make a generalization": before you look at anything else, decide whether a choice is about the category or about one member of it.

A.why: You chose a specific instance. Calling Haitian Creole "a creole language" connects it to the category, but the sentence is still about one language. That makes it an example, not a generalization.

C.why: You chose a comparison of two instances. Naming two creoles and setting them side by side is still talking about individual languages, not making a claim about creoles as a group.

D.why: You picked a choice that sounds broad, but it says more than the notes do. The notes give French and English as sources for two languages only. They never say that every creole draws on one of those two.

stem: Which sentence provides an example of a keystone species?
stimulus:
Notes:
• Ecologists use the term "keystone species" for a species whose effect on its ecosystem is far larger than its numbers would suggest.
• Sea otters are a keystone species in North Pacific kelp forests.
• Sea otters eat sea urchins, which graze on kelp.
• Where otters disappear, urchins multiply and kelp forests can collapse.
choices: A keystone species has an effect on its ecosystem far larger than its numbers.
The sea otter, a keystone species, protects kelp by eating the urchins that graze it.
Sea urchins graze on kelp, and kelp forests can collapse where urchins multiply.
Every ocean ecosystem depends on sea otters to keep its kelp forests from collapsing.
explanation: An example needs two parts: one named instance, and a link from that instance to the category in the goal. Choice B names the sea otter and labels it a keystone species, so it has both parts. You will use this check on Rhetorical Synthesis questions whose goal says "provide an example of" something.

A.why: You chose the definition. It explains what a keystone species is, but it never names one, and an example has to name an instance.

C.why: This choice names specific organisms, but it never connects any of them to the idea of a keystone species. It also leaves out the otter, which is the species the notes call keystone. A named instance only counts as an example if it is tied to the category.

D.why: You picked a sentence about otters that claims much more than the notes support. The notes describe North Pacific kelp forests only. They say nothing about every ocean ecosystem.

stem: Which sentence makes a generalization about tapering?
stimulus:
Notes:
• Tapering means reducing training volume in the days before a competition.
• Studies of swimmers, runners, and cyclists have found that most athletes perform better after a taper of one to three weeks.
• In one study, 12 college swimmers improved their 100-meter times by about 2 percent after a two-week taper.
• In another study, a group of cyclists raised their power output by about 4 percent after tapering.
choices: Twelve college swimmers cut their 100-meter times by about 2 percent after tapering.
Tapered cyclists gained about 4 percent in power, while swimmers gained about 2 percent.
Across several sports, most athletes perform better after a taper of one to three weeks.
Any athlete who tapers for two weeks will improve performance by at least 2 percent.
explanation: Choice C is about "most athletes" across several sports, and no single study or group is its subject. That makes it a claim about tapering in general. In real Rhetorical Synthesis questions, the generalization is often the note that the specific studies support, so look for the sentence that sits above the individual cases.

A.why: You chose one specific study. A result from twelve swimmers is an instance that supports the generalization, but it is not the generalization itself.

B.why: You chose a comparison between two studies. Comparing cyclists to swimmers keeps the sentence at the level of individual cases, not tapering in general.

D.why: This sounds general, but it turns "most athletes" into "any athlete" and turns one study's 2 percent into a guaranteed minimum. The notes support neither change.

stem: Which sentence provides an example of an attenuated vaccine?
stimulus:
Notes:
• Some vaccines contain a live but weakened form of a virus.
• Immunologists call these attenuated vaccines.
• The measles vaccine contains a live, weakened form of the measles virus.
• Other vaccines, such as the injected flu vaccine, contain virus that has been inactivated, or killed.
choices: Attenuated vaccines contain a form of a virus that is live but has been weakened.
The injected flu vaccine contains a form of the flu virus that has been inactivated.
Every vaccine given to children contains a live but weakened form of some virus.
The measles vaccine contains a form of the measles virus that is live but weakened.
explanation: Choice D names one specific vaccine and gives the property that makes a vaccine attenuated: it contains a live but weakened virus. The word "attenuated" does not appear in D, but the notes define attenuated as exactly that property. On real items the goal often uses a term that only one note defines, so match the property, not the word.

A.why: You chose the category statement. It defines attenuated vaccines but never names one, and an example has to name an instance.

B.why: This choice names a specific vaccine, but it is the wrong kind. The notes describe the injected flu vaccine as inactivated, which is the contrasting type, not an attenuated one.

C.why: This makes a sweeping claim the notes don't support. The notes mention measles only, and they say some vaccines are inactivated. Also, this sentence names no specific vaccine, so it cannot be an example anyway.
